name: Learn2Play Bench

scale.notes: questions = 20 game instances, one pinned seed per game template: 10 fixed and 10 re-shuffled games, 5 of them challenge games. Each configuration plays 3 independent trials of 5 episodes (normal games) or 10 (challenge games), giving 375 scored episodes (project website). The paper reports no dialogue count and no context length. The human study has 21-30 participants per game.

metrics: Max (average over trials of peak normalized terminal score)
Mean (average normalized score across evaluated episodes)
Learning Gain (LG: mean of last k_g episodes minus mean of first k_g episodes, k_g = min(3, floor(T_g/2)))
Learning Slope (LS: slope of a linear fit of mean normalized score on episode index)
LS drop (Control LS minus Re-shuffled LS, RQ4 transfer)
notes: v1 (2026-10-06) compares nine OpenCode backbones. v2 (2026-10-08) adds Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, for eleven. Scores are normalized by per-game reference scores (Table 6), and challenge games carry 3x weight. The repo is an anonymous-review snapshot of the 20 games and play.py. It has no licence, no human records, no agent harness and no metric pipeline. Repo IDs differ from the paper's game names (hezu = Roommates, modelkeeper_expert = Model Auditor). An issue requesting a Hugging Face release was open on 2026-10-10.

sources.venue: The arXiv abs page and API have no journal_ref and no comments. The repo README says only 'code snapshot for anonymous peer review' and names no venue. Result: arXiv preprint.
sources.memory_types: procedural_workflow: agents must discover hidden game rules 'by acting, observing textual feedback, and carrying useful experience into later episodes, without updating model weights' (§1). LG and LS 'measure improvement across episodes' (§4.1). The compared methods are experience-memory methods: Memory, Reflexion, EvoTest, ReasoningBank and AWM (§4.2). RQ4 re-shuffled games change the visible instance while keeping the rule, testing whether learned knowledge transfers (§4.5). The other types do not apply. There is no event-recall QA (not episodic) and no weight updates (not parametric, §2). The games are mostly abstract text games such as menus, prediction and social rules, not navigation or manipulation (not embodied).

name: MetaKernelBench

scale.notes: 74 fused-subgraph GPU-kernel problems in six families. Each is posed as a CuTe DSL variant and a TIRx variant, giving 148 variants. With 6 models x 2 transfer directions, the paper reports 888 paired solo-vs-skill-conditioned comparisons. There are no conversations, and no context length is reported.

metrics: Speedup vs eager reference (passing-only geometric mean GM, capped at 100x)
notes: The repo ships 32 of the 74 problems. The other 42 come from nvidia/SOL-ExecBench, whose NVIDIA Evaluation Dataset License forbids redistribution, so users must build them locally with metakernelbench/sol_execbench.py. Running the benchmark needs a Modal account with B200 GPUs and model-provider API keys. The CLI defaults to 3 replicates, while the paper uses single attempts (README: --n-replicates 1). The paper's LLM annotators (unnamed) appear only in the skill and failure analyses, not in the main scoring. Code is Apache-2.0.

name: MLE-InsightBench

scale.notes: questions = the 12 held-out target tasks (one Kaggle competition per domain) used for evaluation. The benchmark has 160 competitions in 12 domains; the other 148 are source competitions used only to assemble insights. Each condition gets 6 runs per task (72 runs), a 12-hour budget and at most 250 agent steps. There are no conversations, and context length does not apply.

metrics: Normalized private-test score (per-task min-max normalized, % change from no-insight baseline)
Task-specific private-test scores via MLE-bench-compatible graders (R2, Fmax, mAA, AUC, SNR, Sharpe, GLL, Brier, MAE, MCC)
Normalized validation score over development time
Number of significant tasks (two-sided Mann-Whitney U, alpha=0.05, Holm-Bonferroni)
notes: Agents are evaluated on 12 held-out Kaggle targets. Insights (12 domain, 148 competition and 16 improvement insights) are assembled offline from the gold-medal solutions and writeups of source competitions, then injected as skills or a playbook. The agent does not accumulate them from its own runs. The paper says the workflow and insights are open-sourced, but arXiv v1 gives no link, and no official repo or dataset was found on GitHub or Hugging Face (checked 2026-10-10). Target tasks need Kaggle competition data.

name: ServeLearnBench

scale.notes: 3,210 = held-out test tasks, the only tasks scored. Each run also serves 4,508 serving tasks with score-only feedback, for 7,718 tasks in total. These are spread over 9 scenarios (Retail/Banking/Pitch × tiers L1–L3) and 53 environment windows. The task stream is not split into conversations. Per-episode budgets are 50 tool calls, 100 turns and 256k output tokens.

metrics: Hidden-Dependent score (mean reward x100 on held-out test tasks)
Avg. H / Avg. F (unweighted means across settings)
API cost and token cost per task
notes: Data is in the GitHub repo under dataset/; no Hugging Face release was found (checked 2026-10-10). The repo implements only the Blind, Oracle and RAG methods. Results for Mem0, SkillOpt, Continual Harness and Prime appear only in docs/leaderboard.csv. Runs need an OpenAI-compatible endpoint with native tool calling. Pitch is scored by an LLM judge (default glm-5p3-flash at high reasoning effort). The task 'evaluator' fields and windows.json reveal the hidden policies, so they must not be shown to agents. Licence: Apache-2.0.

name: ConsolidationBench

scale.notes: The paper reports no instance or question counts. Experience streams are generated procedurally in medium and hard configurations, with raw experience mass 7.3x/9.4x the reference budget. The leaderboard ranks 10 policies (medium). A separate external-validity study used 12 policies and 2,532 answer cells on LoCoMo multi-hop and 2WikiMultiHopQA, which are not part of ConsolidationBench.

metrics: Reuse / Transfer (success on novel composite tasks)
Consolidation Quality Score (CQS; original multiplicative CQS0 and graded geometric-mean CQS with epsilon=0.05)
Governance checks: false rules admitted from poison decoys (G1), rollback recovery (G2), ledger completeness (G3), CQS0 retained (G4)
notes: ConsolidationBench is Phase 3 of a four-phase research paper. No code, data or generator is released. Section 7 holds the benchmark-generator parameters (cluster-type constants, oracle-computation specifics) under "controlled release": reviewers and collaborators can request them, under terms. The benchmark therefore cannot be regenerated from the paper alone. The paper names no base LLM. The authors report that CQS does not predict real transfer accuracy (pooled Spearman rho = -0.24). The PDF header reads "June 2026"; arXiv v1 is dated 2026-09-26. The paper is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

name: Cross-lingual Unlearning Tensor

scale.notes: questions = 4,000 TOFU forget10+retain90 English source questions (App. A.3), each queried across 174 language-script pairs. There are 52,916 English paraphrases over 25 types, and translated paraphrases in 40 languages (1,690 rows per language). Held-out forget sets A/B have 400 QA pairs each. The LORELEI set has 100 news documents in 8 languages. LUME is also used. No single total query count is reported.

metrics: Oracle-normalized residual access R = (p_U - p_O)/(p_FT - p_O) (removal = 1 - R)
LLM-judged generation outcomes: full leakage, partial leakage / any disclosure, retained recovery, code-switching, gibberish
Spearman rank correlation of subset rankings (COVER analysis)
notes: The full benchmark data (translated QA pairs and paraphrases) is not public. The paper and the repo README say it will be released after peer review. As checked on 2026-10-10, the official repo had a single commit dated 2026-09-29. It holds only an interactive dashboard (index.html) and aggregated per-cell score tables (parquet/CSV) in data/, with no evaluation code. The benchmark builds on TOFU (10% forget split) and LUME. The paper also proposes the COVER source-selection method.

name: EmbodiedMemory-Bench (EMem-Bench)

scale.notes: 2,554 episodes, each = one multimodal interaction history (2.0-4.5 sessions) plus one target task: Passive Observation 1,036, Dynamic Tracking 1,052, Interaction Failure 263, Experience Generalization 203; 1,118 scenes. GPT-5.4-mini full_context averages 41,770 input tokens/episode (800-episode subset, Table 3). Fixed 800-episode subset (200/family) used for analyses; single 'all' split.

metrics: Success Rate (SR), per task family and equal-weighted macro average
notes: The code lives in the embodied_memory/ subfolder of the ZJU-OmniAI/Embodied-Omni monorepo (subfolder Apache-2.0; repo root MulanPSL-2.0). The Hugging Face data is ungated, CC BY-NC 4.0, with a single 'all' split and no train/val split. Episode text was later translated to English; the original-language version is at revision 28694bf. Evaluation needs the AI2-THOR 5.0 simulator. The main full_context setting gives a text history plus only the current RGB frame; memory systems ingest historical RGB frames. The paper also introduces the EMem memory system and the EMem-8B policy.

name: EvoPathBench

scale.avg_context_length: 5 episodes per stream; 24 market steps / 3 decisions per episode
scale.notes: conversations = 1,800 longitudinal task streams: 600 per template (Accumulation, Interference, Reversal), 100 per template-family cell, 900 per market layer. questions = 3,600 held-out probe episodes. The release holds 4,800 episode specifications in total, which adds 1,200 learning/update episodes. Each stream has 5 update opportunities and 6 checkpoints (K0-K5). Counted 2026-10-10.

metrics: Episode score (risk-adjusted terminal wealth ratio with violation and drawdown penalties; App. B.5 Eq. 9)
Capability Evolution Gain: CEG_N (near-distribution) and CEG_T (transfer) (Eq. 3, Table 2)
Backward transfer (BWT), forgetting rate, conditional loss, CVaR_0.1 (Sec. 4.5, Table 7)
Commit rate, best gain, selection gap, harmful rate, missed rate (Table 4)
Agreement, Capture, Precision, Recall of update selection (Table 5)
notes: Single finance track: semi-synthetic markets calibrated on public Binance Spot data. The raw market archives are not redistributed. The paper runs 10 memory/skill self-evolution conditions on two backbones, Qwen3.8-Max and Kimi-K3. Inference needs an OpenAI-compatible API. The README lists a results/main/ folder that was absent from the repo tree on 2026-10-10. analysis/evaluate_dimensions.py hard-codes 108 evolution paths per template, against 600 released streams per template. The paper does not state the size of its evaluated subset. Licence: MIT.

name: IDUnlearn-Bench

scale.notes: 4,860 evaluation-only VQA probes (81 per individual) over 60 synthetic individuals, in 4 task families / 9 subtasks (AA 2,520; IA 1,320; IB 480; IR 540). There is also a separate 10,050-QA supervision set used to inject the profiles by LoRA fine-tuning, plus 1,442 images. Splits are by identity: Forget-1 and Forget-5, with the remaining identities as the retain set. These are single probes, not conversations.

metrics: Forget residual (normalized answer-containment accuracy, %, per task family AA/IA/IB/IR)
Retain utility (normalized answer-containment accuracy, %, per task family)
notes: Benchmark for unlearning individual identities from VLMs. Synthetic profiles are fine-tuned into the weights with LoRA, then unlearned. It builds on the authors' MultiPriv data. The repo and the HF dataset (Apache-2.0, not gated) contain only data: per-person images, bench_VQA.json and finetune_VQA.json. They include no fine-tuning, unlearning or scoring code. Counted on 2026-10-10, the release matches the paper: 4,860 probes, 10,050 supervision QAs and 1,442 images. The release uses 12 fine-grained task labels rather than the paper's 9 subtask names.

name: VibeMemBench

scale.notes: questions = 111 SWE-style coding targets (bug fixes, feature requests, interface changes, configuration work) from 90 SWE-rebench V2 repositories. conversations = 3,634 completed history trajectories from earlier tasks in the same repositories, which memory systems ingest. Each condition runs 4 seeds (444 target-seed runs). No train/test split. The paper gives no length statistics for the history trajectories.

metrics: Resolved (share of target-seed runs whose declared executable test predicate passes), with 95% bootstrap CI over targets
Paired memory effect (memory-on minus memory-off Resolved)
notes: The official repo directory was checked on 2026-10-10. It held only a placeholder README ("Coming"), with no task histories, test predicates or evaluation code, although paper §6 says these will be released. Targets were kept only when injected experience improved results for a reference setting (deepseek-v4-flash + MiniSWEAgent). Results are then reported on five held-out solvers. The paper evaluates four memory systems: Mem0, SimpleMem, MemoryOS and A-MEM. The paper is licensed CC BY 4.0.

The paper does not print repo/data URLs; the repo and HF card link back to arXiv 2609.32607. Four latest_state questions do not nest strictly across budgets. name: ContinualSkillBench

scale.notes: questions = 500 subtasks: 5 domains (Healthcare, Law, Mathematics, Finance, Office) x 100 ordered subtasks, each domain solved as one sequential stream. There is no conversation unit, so conversations is null. The repo also ships science-100 (100 subtasks, not in the paper) and per-domain independent-trial splits. The paper reports no context-length statistics.

metrics: Raw reward (mean score over the 100 subtasks of a domain)
Normalized reward (only tasks with valid outputs under both Sequential and Independent)
Per-subtask scoring: exact match, token-level F1, numeric with tolerance, rubric-based LLM judge, programmatic tests
Skill invocation frequency and final skill repository size
Generated-skill quality score (format x content, judged by GPT-4.1-mini)
notes: The paper version has five domains (Healthcare, Law, Mathematics, Finance, Office), each with 100 ordered subtasks. The repo (a single commit dated 2026-08-04, Apache-2.0) also ships a science-100 domain that is not in the paper, plus independent-trial variants. Rubric-judged subtasks (25-68 per domain) need an LLM judge that the paper does not name. The repo's sequential agents default to claude-sonnet-4-6, and the example configs override it. Tasks are repackaged from third-party benchmarks (e.g. TAT-QA, HealthBench, LegalBench, Harvey), whose own licences apply. Running them needs Docker, and some need internet access.

scale.notes: 60 = admitted three-session trap sequences in the v2 confirmatory fold (S1/S2 inject evidence, S3 trap); questions = their 60 S3 trap tasks, each run with 3 seeds (180 S3 cells per condition). name: GDPevo

scale.notes: questions = 240 business tasks in 24 task groups (V1: 120 tasks/12 groups in CRM, ERP and finance; V2 adds 120 tasks/12 groups in healthcare, legal and data work). Each group has 5 training tasks for evolution and 5 held-out test tasks; accuracy is scored on the 120 test tasks, 3 runs each. There are no conversations. The repo has 120 train and 120 test task directories (counted on 2026-10-10).

metrics: Accuracy (macro-averaged rubric score on held-out test tasks, mean of 3 runs)
notes: The benchmark evaluates agent self-evolution. Agents distil a SKILL.md from 5 training tasks and reuse it on 5 held-out test tasks under four supervision modes: base, fewshot, self and reflect-3. The paper evaluates Codex/GPT-5.5 and Claude Code with Opus-4.8, GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Preview. A full run is agent-orchestrated: Codex drives Dockerised environments by following README prompts, so there is no single CLI command. The data is in the GitHub repo (Apache-2.0); task_group_022 uses a Git LFS SQLite file. Paper results use V2 (240 tasks).

name: MemToC

scale.notes: 6,504 evaluation episodes = 542 quality-controlled factual questions x 4 tool conditions (correct, near-incorrect, tool error, no return) x 3 instruction formulations. A far-incorrect condition covers 443 questions. Released files hold 575 questions x 5 conditions (2,875 episodes per formulation). Not a conversational benchmark. No context length is reported.

notes: The benchmark tests arbitration between a model's parametric (closed-book) answer and a controlled tool return whose correctness is known. Closed-book answers are elicited per model, so case sizes differ by model. The repo (Apache-2.0) ships the benchmark JSONs, per-episode scoring decisions without raw generations, and a harness that re-derives the paper's numbers. It has no script that runs a new model end to end. The paper's 6,504 count excludes 33 of the 575 released questions.

name: MemTrapBench

scale.notes: 1,050 instances, each one multi-turn dialogue history plus one final query: 350 Cognitive Bias, 350 Task Boundary, 200 Safety, 150 Trauma. The repo files hold 1,050 items (counted 2026-10-10), with a mean history of about 29.5 turns (~18.4K characters). Ablations use subsets, and the AdaptiveMem experiments sample 200 instances.

metrics: Average score (%) and drop vs. no-memory baseline
judge_model: GPT-5.2 (primary judge; Claude-Sonnet-4.6 used only to check judge consistency)
notes: arXiv v1 is marked 'Work in progress'. Repo files map to the paper's scenarios as follows: Cognitive Bias = Inertia_150 + number_game_200, Task Boundary = hallucination_150 + unclear_200, Trauma = hurt_150, Safety = poison_200. Retrieved-memory outputs from the evaluated frameworks (LightMem, MemOS, SimpleMem, EverMemOS) are not released, so users must supply them. Judging needs a paid API (default GPT-5.2 via OpenRouter). The repo has no licence file (checked 2026-10-10). The paper says it is related to, but distinct from, MemSyco-Bench.

name: PAST-Bench

scale.notes: 26 = task-family scenarios (ordered sequences of fresh-session episodes); 204 = episodes across Memory (5/41), Procedural Reuse (8/64), Information Gathering (6/48), Update (7/51). Each family mixes cold, learn, eval-near/far and control episodes. The repo has 211 episode directories with task.yaml; family.yaml episode lists sum to 204 (counted 2026-10-10).

metrics: Per-episode task score s_e = safety gate x (0.80 completion + 0.20 tool-error robustness)
Self-evolution gap Delta (persistence-on minus matched persistence-off score, macro-averaged over families/capabilities)
Mechanism-evidence score Mech (mean of write precision, recall accuracy, update correctness, retention horizon, 1 - pollution rate)
notes: Agent benchmark of cross-session improvement: agents run ordered fresh-session task sequences with persistence on/off; tasks are synthetic, using local mock services (gmail, slack, calendar, CRM, etc.). Running it requires Docker and model API keys; the default judge is MiniMax-M2.7 (config.yaml). The repo bundles third-party agents (Hermes, nanobot, ZeroClaw, Agent Zero) under their own licences; PAST-Bench code is Apache-2.0. The paper also introduces Hermes+, an agent framework. Paper results average 3 runs.

name: S3Gym

scale.notes: Not QA/dialogue-based: 7 text games (Chess, Minesweeper, Nullify, Tetris, Snake, PvZ, Trust Evolution). Per model-game-pathway: 30 permissive exploration episodes, then 3 strict-mode evaluation episodes at each of 11 checkpoints (0,3,...,30); max 5-64 steps/episode; History-ICL input capped at 100,000 tokens. Self-judging analysis: 98 runs, 116,117 transitions. Training study: Qwen3-8B, 20 checkpoints.

metrics: Delta Final (final minus initial score, training study)
NMAE (normalized mean absolute error of self-judged vs verifier reward)
Judgment-improvement correlation rho(A,g), rho(-E,g) and tertile gaps
notes: No official code or data found (checked 2026-10-10): paper and project page (self-developing-agents.github.io, a static page also covering Aspire and HarnessDev) give no repo or dataset link, though the paper mentions a "released implementation". Games follow the KORGym paradigm. Main context-level results cover 7 proprietary models (History ICL vs Summary Memory); the parameter-training pathway is a separate auxiliary study on Qwen3-8B. Scores use different scales per game; AUC+ is comparable only within a game.

name: AgentStream

scale.notes: 300 = 50 tasks sampled from each of six benchmarks (AppWorld test-challenge, BFCL multi-turn base, BrowseComp-Plus, HLE, SWE-bench Verified, Tau2 telecom). The same set is run as Isolated, Sequential and Interleaved streams over 3 ordering seeds (42/44/46). No conversation count applies. Context length is not reported; vanilla runs average 9.5 (GPT-5.4) and 21.1 (Gemini 3.1 Pro) agent steps per task.

metrics: Task accuracy (%) from each benchmark's native scoring pipeline, averaged over 3 seeds
Evolution gain Δ = Perf(M,Q,S) − Perf(M,Q,∅) over the vanilla baseline
Top-1 rate (share of configurations where a scenario is best)
Per-task cost ($) and relative cost overhead
Average agent steps and Δ steps (%)
notes: AgentStream is an evaluation protocol over tasks from existing benchmarks. It has no standalone dataset. Tasks are pulled from the upstream benchmarks via `exgentic install --benchmark` and selected with fixed seed 42 in scripts/utils/task_ordering.py. HLE data (cais/hle on Hugging Face) is gated. Runs need LLM API keys, with GPT-5.4 acting as judge and user simulator. The paper's footnote links a mirror at microsoft/Sico/labs/AgentStream (MIT), and the arXiv comment links Jasper-Yan/AgentStream (Apache-2.0). arXiv has v1 (2026-07-31) and v2 (2026-09-27), with the same setup.

name: CAPA

scale.notes: 60 = user-ambiguity cells (user trajectories), 10 sessions each, 600 coding sessions in total. In each cell, 5 resolved sessions form the history and 5 are held out. 300 = held-out evaluation sessions, solved under an 8-turn budget. Held-out difficulty, from a no-history reference run: 97 simple, 89 medium, 114 complex. The tasks derive from HumanEval. The paper does not report token or context length.

notes: CAPA = Cross-Session Adaptation to Personalized Ambiguity. Sessions are synthetic, generated in an LLM-simulated environment (AmbiSimu) from HumanEval tasks. The paper names no generator, simulator or judge model, but the repo's frozen data says the history dialogues are GPT-5.5. Models run without history and with same-user history. The paper links no code. Repo xuzijan/Synthetic-data is attributed to the first author (account name, results identical to Tables 1/3/5). It uses internal names (PACI-Bench, DialogRL v02), has no licence and commits no runner for the frozen data.

scale.notes: questions = 194 code prompts (100 SALLM Python + 94 CWEval JS/C++/C/Go), each paired with one insecure-preference memory prompt. name: MemOps

scale.avg_context_length: 60,821 tokens (avg., long-context setting; adjacent setting 2,557 tokens)
scale.notes: 403 evidence conversations (3 segments each; 9,672 turns) over 100 topics; 2,006 unique QA pairs, each asked in an adjacent and a long-context (UltraChat-injected) setting = 4,012 evaluation instances. Five operation types, six probe types. Long-context max is 68,309 tokens.

notes: Data ships inside the GitHub repo (MIT); no separate dataset page. The long-context files total about 178 MB. Counts were taken on 2026-10-10 and match the paper: 403 files, 2,006 QA pairs, 4,012 instances. The repo's eval script covers long-context, no-context and BM25 RAG variants (vanilla/delete/rewrite). The paper's Mem0, MemOS and Temp-LoRA baselines are not included. The run and judge steps need an OpenAI-compatible API. The default answer models in the shell launchers differ from those in the paper.

name: MemSecBench

scale.notes: questions = 310 linked lifecycle cases (Code & Science 113, Daily Life 107, Office Work 90) from 48 contexts with 6-10 cases each. Each case compiles into Write, Execute and Forget stage tasks, 930 in total. The paper reports no conversation count or context length. Main results cover 24 harness x backend x LLM configurations, each run on all 310 cases. A Chinese mirror of the corpus exists.

metrics: Per-checkpoint pass rates (W1 Write Operation, W2 Persistence, E1 Recall Exposure, E2 Adoption, E3 Externalization, F1 Repair, F2 Benign Preservation)
notes: The arXiv v1 paper gives no code or data link. As of 2026-10-10 none was found on GitHub, Hugging Face or alphaXiv, although the paper mentions a released case-authoring Skill and released cases. GPT-5.5 authored the cases under human review. Experiments use the English task packages; a Chinese mirror also exists. Running the benchmark needs Docker, the OpenClaw/Hermes harnesses, the Mem0/Mem0-Graph/A-MEM backends and simulated services (web gateway, Mailpit, GitLab). Each configuration-case pair was run once.

name: MERIT

scale.notes: Tasks are generated procedurally from seeds, so there is no fixed item count. Each (domain x tier x memory condition) cell has 10 arcs x 5 episodes, with a dependent ratio of 0.5. There are 3 domains and 3 difficulty tiers. 23,440 scored episodes in total: a 9,940-episode pilot (starter and real generations) plus a 13,500-episode 3-model full grid. D1 also has a corruption sweep.

metrics: Metered tokens and dollar cost per episode
notes: A benchmark generator and harness, not a static dataset. Tasks come from seeded code (merit/), and full results and traces are committed under runs/. There is no Hugging Face dataset. Code is MIT-licensed. The repo README still gives $44.82 total cost, while arXiv v1 gives a corrected $42.57. Commits from Sept 2026 add failure-anatomy and counterfactual-ordering analyses that are not in arXiv v1. Memory corruption is framed as staleness robustness, not as attacks. The answer key of the MUR audit sample is withheld.

name: PM-Bench

scale.notes: Main set is one fixed seven-day scenario (data/synthetic_week_v9.json). 81 is the number of scored executable tasks; there are 83 task definitions in all (57 event-based, 26 time-based, 7 cross-day), plus 11 update events, 11 state channels and 74 lures. metrics: Set-F1 (macro and micro, over prospective action selections)
Diagnostic breakdown: hit/on-time, late, miss, false alarm, wrong-content, update violation, dependency violation, exact-set match
notes: Tests prospective memory: carrying out deferred intentions at a future cue or time, including after cancel, override or reschedule updates and when cues sit in hidden state channels that must be queried. Only one deterministic synthetic week (v9) is released, and every reported result uses it. On 2026-10-10 the repo had no licence file. The README points to runs/March_ALL_results_v9/, but the folder is runs/all_results_v9/. The abstract credits 65.1% F1 to a GPT-5.4 agent, but Table 2 gives 65.1 as the optional-heartbeat macro Set-F1 averaged across all 8 models.

name: RUMBA

scale.notes: 85 timestamped user-assistant dialogues (12-85 sessions and 180-998 utterances each) and 1,543 QA pairs (14-22 per dialogue, 17 base types). An aligned English translation has the same 85 dialogues and 1,543 QA pairs; both counts were checked in the HF jsonl files on 2026-10-10. Average length is ~341K characters for RU and ~321K for EN (Table 4). No token count is given.

metrics: LLM-as-Judge accuracy (primary; judge labels 2-3 count as correct)
F1 (per-question bag-of-words F1, max over references)
judge_model: POLLUX (ai-forever/pollux-judge-32b) for Russian; DeepSeek-R1 for English
notes: The main benchmark is in Russian, with an aligned English translation. Russian and English use different judges (POLLUX vs DeepSeek-R1), so their scores are not directly comparable. User turns were written by 26 human contributors and assistant turns were generated by GigaChat Max. Question types include UpdatingInfo and DeleteInfo ("forget it" requests). Dialogue length is reported in characters only. Repo and data are MIT-licensed. Each HF row embeds the full dialogue, so the files are about 0.98 GB (ru) and 0.54 GB (en). The mem0 baseline needs a paid mem0 account.

Delta / Delta_L (accuracy gain from tutorial over the w/o-Tutorial baseline)
notes: arXiv v1 links no code or data. The self-described official HF dataset holds Apache-2.0 annotations plus tutorial/target clips and a concat script, but no evaluation script. Some long-setting distractors reference Video-MME videos that are not hosted there. The HF card claims NeurIPS 2026 Datasets & Benchmarks, which could not be verified; v1 was compiled with the preprint option. The paper is internally inconsistent: 11 vs 8 task types, and "up to 2-hour" vs "2-3 hour" streams. GitHub lark-png/SLVMBench is a README-only placeholder.

The paper also calls the Long setting 'episodic memory capability' (§3.3), but its questions test skill application rather than event recall.

name: AFTER

scale.notes: questions = 382 tasks (318 single-skill, 64 multi-skill) across 6 roles and 22 skills. The paper defines 50/25/25 train/validation/test splits per (role, skill) cell and reports results on a 185-task train split. The public release has 129 test-split tasks (de 27, ds 23, genai 22, swe 22, infra 19, pm 16). There are no conversations, and context length is not reported.

metrics: M1: average partial progress (fraction of verifier tests passed per task, averaged over attempts)
M2: full-pass rate (fraction of attempts passing all tests; primary metric)
Token usage and dollar cost (Appendix G, auto-agent runs)
notes: The public release (Hugging Face dataset plus a co-author's GitHub mirror, Apache-2.0, not gated) has only 129 tasks, all marked split "test" in tasks/manifest.json (counted 2026-10-10). The paper and README describe 382 tasks with 50/25/25 train/validation/test splits. The paper's Evolution harness and the train/validation tasks are not released. The repo provides only per-task data generators, reference solutions and pytest verifiers. The paper is titled "Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents: Control, Adaptation, and Evaluation".

name: AhaBench

scale.notes: No single item count is reported. Aha-Puzzle: 7 puzzle identities x 4 languages x 3 repeats, giving 84 cold/endpoint pairs and 588 curriculum episodes per model. Aha-Euler: 50 single-step + 90 graph-composition tasks (140 in benchmark_manifest.json); the main teaching contrast uses 50 single-step requests per condition. Aha-Vending: 5 incident-setting seeds of up to 365 simulated days per model.

metrics: Endpoint gain (trace-free score minus cold score on same targets)
Aha-Euler held-out exact-match accuracy (cold / full teaching / answer-only teaching)
Aha-Vending terminal profit, completion, survival days, termination mode
Time-averaged profit, maximum drawdown, early/late 90-day earning rates
v1 scorecard: Initial Score, Post-Experience Score, Learning Lift
notes: The title and framing changed between arXiv v1 (2026-06-30), which leads with an Initial/Post-Experience/Learning Lift scorecard, and v2 (2026-09-21), which uses each component's own metrics; the README keeps the old scorecard as a legacy view. The three components are Aha-Puzzle, Aha-Euler and Aha-Vending (a simulator inspired by Vending-Bench). Experience reaches the fixed-weight agents in context. The repo has no root licence: Puzzle is Apache-2.0, Euler and Vending are MIT. Runs need OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and Puzzle also needs a host/judge LLM. No model outputs are packaged.

name: Continual Learning Bench (CL-Bench)

scale.avg_context_length: on the order of tens of instances per task sequence
scale.notes: 6 = task sequences (one default schedule per domain). 301 = total instances, summed from the per-task counts in Tables 2-7: Blind Spectrum Monitoring 90 scans, Codebase Adaptation 19 issues, Cohort Studies 20, Database Exploration 40 questions, Exploitable Poker 120 hands, Sales Prediction 12. The paper text says '300+'. Each instance has up to 40 steps. The repo also has extra variants and schedules (e.g. a 30-question multi_group variant and a quick_test schedule).

metrics: Gain (stateful reward minus same system's stateless reward, per instance and cumulative)
Normalized reward (vs. stateless GPT-5.4 ICL reference and task r_max)
Normalized gain (fraction of own learning headroom captured)

Task-specific rewards: mean IoU (BSM), step-efficiency (Codebase), KL-based information gain in bits (Cohort), query-budget efficiency / regret (Database), big blinds per hand (Poker), WAPE skill (Sales)
notes: A continual-learning benchmark built from six expert-validated agentic task sequences. Memory is scored as the gain of a stateful run over a stateless run, not as recall QA. Running it needs model-provider API keys, Docker (for Codebase Adaptation and Sales Prediction) and `clbench setup`, which fetches the Database Exploration SQLite files from Hugging Face (not gated). Repo v1.0 was released 2026-05-04 under Apache-2.0. A 2026-07-19 commit changed how the leaderboard script normalizes Cohort Studies rewards, so the leaderboard may differ from paper Table 1. The paper did not evaluate parametric methods.

name: DMV-Bench

scale.notes: questions = recall probes on Gemini 2.5 Flash summed over the J=5/10/15 cells and the Monte Carlo J=50 pilot (2,762+5,003+25,196+2,449). Qwen2.5-VL-7B gives 15,361. Probes come from each back-end's own browsing of a 1,000-product catalogue, so there is no fixed set of chains. arXiv v1 reported 46,265/18,588. Sessions run 22–28 steps.

metrics: Task success rate (TSR; exact match on the product URL)
TSR stratified by recall reach r
notes: An interactive benchmark: running it requires the local Next.js storefront (env/frontend) plus the agent harness. Probes and trajectories are generated at run time from each VLM back-end's browsing, so probe counts vary and no probe file is released. The 1,000 cued and 1,000 base catalogue images are an ungated Apache-2.0 Hugging Face dataset. The paper also proposes DualMem, and its external baselines are '-lite' re-implementations. Probe counts in arXiv v2 differ from v1. Scoring is by URL match, with no LLM judge.

Its README dataset link (datasets/Aiden0526/EvoArena) does not resolve; the data is in the HF collection.

name: FinEvolveBench

The full 300-day dataset, announced for September 2026, was absent when counted on 2026-10-10. The released pipeline disables experience operations. News is Chinese-language.

name: ForgetEval

scale.notes: 385 = adversarial layer ForgetEval-Adv (132 hand-crafted + 253 DeepSeek-V3-drafted, oracle-validated; 10 attack categories). This is the main surface for the 13-configuration comparison. Each case is one final recall query after scripted mutations. There is also a 1000-case templated suite (5 families x 200, seed=42, 4 distractors per case) and a 77-case external-authored subset (Appendix R). No conversations are involved.

metrics: Pass rate (deterministic substring match on top-10 recall: must_contain present, must_not_contain absent), per family / per attack category / overall
N/A-excluded vs strict-denominator pass rate (N/A for unsupported primitives)
notes: The cases ship as Python code in the repo (generate.py, adversarial.py, adversarial_generated.py), with no separate data files. A count on 2026-10-10 found 132 + 253 = 385 adversarial cases, matching Table 2, but run.py's help text still says 64. The repo was not found to contain the 77-case external subset, the IAA/audit files, or the LLM-hook runner. The repo's paper.pdf is an earlier 23-page version under a different title. The author also develops Lethe, one of the evaluated systems. HF dbaysal/ForgetEval is an unrelated code dataset. The licence is MIT.

name: GateMem

scale.notes: 91 long-form multi-party episodes (Medical 21, Office 17, Education 30, Household 23) and 2,218 hidden checkpoints: 728 utility, 727 access-control, 763 active-forgetting. notes: The release is open-label: the hidden annotation fields (query_type, expected_action, judge_spec, leak_targets) ship with the data, and methods must not use them at inference. name: HUSH-Bench

scale.notes: 2,400 single-turn benign probe cases. That is 10 personas x 4 probe families x 60. The 10 personas come from 10 LoCoMo source dialogues augmented with assistant-user histories. Primary matrix: 4 generators x 5 memory conditions = 48,000 scored responses. Controls use 600, 2,400 or 40 cases per model. The invitation contrast uses 200 pairs per generator. History length is not reported.

metrics: Unsolicited History Integration Score (UIS, 0-100, higher is worse)
Exact-target exposure rate (marked disclosure reaches generator)
Over-scope severity and binary over-scope rate
Secondary dimensions: relationship-maintenance agreement, affective intensity, assistant centrality
judge_model: GPT-5.4 (primary judge); Claude-Opus-4.6 as second-judge robustness check
notes: arXiv v1 (2026-06-04) was titled "When Should Memory Stay Silent..." and called the benchmark RBI-Eval (Relevant-But-Inappropriate Evaluation), scored with a separation score. v2 (2026-08-03) renamed it HUSH-Bench and introduced UIS. The paper says data, retrieval outputs and protocols will be released upon acceptance. No official repo or dataset was found when checked on 2026-10-10. The benchmark tests one conservative memory-use policy and is English and text-only. Memory systems tested: Mem0, A-Mem, MemU.

name: MedEvoEval

scale.notes: 700 = processed Chinese MedQA-derived simulated outpatient cases (each run as one interactive episode and scored once). Splits: 500 longitudinal-stream cases (ten 50-case stages; conditions E0-E3), 100 held-out transfer cases (H0/H3), 100 cross-sectional cases (80-case model-comparison subset). A 100-episode MDT study is also reported. The artifact reportedly adds 3,103 trajectories and 3,386 step samples.

metrics: Outcome score S = 0.5*diagnostic quality + 0.3*evidence consistency + 0.2*management quality
Utility U (0.6*S minus turn, test and invalid-test cost terms)
Learning gain (LG, late minus early stage mean)
notes: Chinese-language, MedQA-derived cases. The paper describes a released artifact (src/medevoeval runner, configs, scoring and analysis scripts, MedEvoEval-MedQA-700 data), but the paper, arXiv page and NeurIPS page give no repo or dataset URL. No public copy was found when checked on 2026-10-10, and the author's GitHub profile lists the code as "TODO". Memory consists of IF-THEN/IF-AVOID rule cards written by the manager and retrieved top-K. The paper does not name the manager (judge) LLM for each study.

name: MemAudit (formerly MEMPROBE)

scale.avg_context_length: 2.4–2.5 turns per episode on average (31 episodes per user, 25-turn cap)
scale.notes: 50 = synthetic users, each a persistent-memory trajectory of 31 leak-controlled assistance tasks (1,550 episodes per system). 1,550 = hidden user-state recovery targets (31 per user: 7 skill, 7 knowledge, 7 episodic, 5 self-model, 5 assistance-preference), each scored under full-store and top-5 access. Dialogues are regenerated for each evaluated system. There is no train/test split.

metrics: Category-balanced recovery/reconstruction score B (0-1, judge scale {0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1}) under full-store (dump_all) and top-k=5 (retrieve) access
Per-category recovery (skill, knowledge, episodic, self-model, assistance preference)
Memory footprint E (number of items, chars per item)
Failure-attribution counts and recovery rate Recovered/(Recovered+Memory)
notes: arXiv v1 (2026-06-23) was titled MEMPROBE. From v2 (2026-09-18) it is MemAudit, and the repo was renamed from sora1998/MemProbe to sora1998/MEMAUDIT-bench. It is unrelated to MEMAUDIT (arXiv 2605.02199). A gpt-5.4-mini user simulator generates the dialogues at evaluation time, so reruns need OpenAI API access, and Mem-T also needs a local Mem-T-4B server. The repo's main branch has an updated simulator; the paper code and results are on the paper-v1 branch. The data are synthetic and CC BY 4.0.

name: MIST

scale.avg_context_length: 8 turns per conversation (~41 words/turn MIST-Science, ~37 words/turn MIST-Moral)

Five chat regimes each produce their own histories; incorrect-helpful is the main one. 19 MMLU Medical items are excluded from the sycophancy denominator.

metrics: Strict sycophancy rate (share of zero-shot-correct answers that switch to the biased option)
Correction rate (sycophancy metric reversed, Correct-Supportive regime)
notes: The name expands to "Memory Influence on Sycophancy Tests". Data and code are not public: the paper (v2 App. C) says the datasets and codebase will be released on publication, and none were found as of 2026-10-10. Mem0, MemOS and Zep were run through their hosted enterprise APIs in March 2026, so the numbers may not reproduce. v2 (2026-08-24) replaces v1's turn and word statistics with a Prolific realism study and adds MMLU-leakage handling. This benchmark is separate from MemSyco-Bench and PersistBench.

name: MPBench
venue: ICML 2026 Workshop on Agents in the Wild (AIWILD)

scale.notes: questions = adversarial test cases across 6 attack classes and 7 domains (paper Table 7: 5 classes x 600, plus 240 Skill-Procedure Insertion cases for HERMES only). A further 2,997 benign examples are used to measure defense FPR. Each case is a task session (write phase) followed by a retrieval query. It contains no dialogue sessions, and the paper does not report context length.

metrics: Retrieval Success Rate (RSR, cross-session influence, conditioned on ASR)
Detection rate by attack signal strength
notes: Workshop paper. The arXiv paper does not link the official repo (Apache-2.0); the first author's website does. The repo holds only two JSONL data files, with no agent harness, judge prompts or eval code. Counted on 2026-10-10: 3,241 adversarial records (line 1080 holds two concatenated objects) and 2,999 benign, against the paper's 3,240 and 2,997. Released attack_type labels (e.g. fact_injection, experience_injection) differ from the paper's class names. Results use GPT-OSS-120B on the OpenClaw and HERMES agents.

name: OmniGameArena

scale.notes: Not a QA set: 12 UE5 games (7 Solo, 3 PvP, 2 Coop). Cold start: N=5 episodes per (agent, game), 12 agents, PvP over all pairings. IDC (arXiv v1): LastStand and SharedFloor, R=10 rounds x K=5 episodes, 4 agents, 3 held-out variants per game. Released environment: 60 maps (origin + Var1-Var4 per game).

metrics: Normalized game progress score in [0,1] (per-game formulas, Table 1)
PvP Player-1 win rate over all pairings
IDC round score S_r (mean episode score per round) and curve [S_0..S_R]
Transfer gain V_best - V_0 and % change on held-out variants
Actions per episode and score per action (PDQ vs LCRT, appendix)
notes: This is a game-playing benchmark for VLM agents. Memory is tested only through the IDC protocol: a reflector-written skill prompt (at most 1200 tokens) and a notebook (at most 2000 tokens) persist across rounds, then the skill is applied to held-out variants. arXiv v1 runs IDC on 2 games, 4 agents and 3 variants. The repo README and project page describe IDC on all 12 games, 6 models and Var1-Var4. The UE5 builds are ungated Apache-2.0 zips on Hugging Face (about 2.9 GB for Linux, about 2.7 GB for Windows). Linux needs a GPU with Vulkan SM6 support.

name: SEAGym

scale.notes: 55 = held-out in-domain test tasks (Terminal-Bench 2.0 + HLE text-only Math/Physics). The main split also has 80 train tasks (5 epochs, batch size 20; also replayed for forgetting), 35 frozen update-validation tasks and 80 HLE CS/AI + Engineering OOD transfer tasks. Not a dialogue benchmark. Paper Table 7 lists 80/35/50 for the HLE-only source ablation.

metrics: Fix/Forget task churn counts and rates
Token usage / tool calls / wall-clock time / cost
notes: An evaluation environment (protocol + splits), not a new dataset. It evaluates self-evolving agent harnesses such as the ACE skillbook, the TF-GRPO experience store and AHE harness edits on Terminal-Bench 2.0 + HLE tasks run through Harbor. The repo ships task indexes and split manifests but no task content. Users must provide Harbor task trees for terminal-bench-2 and hle, plus DeepSeek and E2B API keys. The released paper configs, checked 2026-10-10, define only the 80/35/55 train/val/ID-test views; OOD and replay views are not configured. Harbor's HLE verifier uses an LLM judge that the paper does not name.

name: SubtleMemory

scale.notes: 10 = persona-level long user-agent histories (one per split). 1,522 = evaluation instances (QAs), derived from 1,090 relation-controlled variant sets (361 complementary, 352 nuanced, 377 contradictory). Released data (counted 2026-10-10) has 1,090 records holding 1,522 QAs: 707 user-related and 815 non-user-related. It also has 2,364 sessions in total.

metrics: Answer correctness rate (binary LLM-as-judge correctness, reported by relation type/subtype and overall)
notes: Text-only, synthetic data. User-related seeds come from PersonaMem-v2 preference profiles, but this is a separate benchmark. The data is in the repo and on Hugging Face (Apache-2.0, not gated). It is split into persona_0 to persona_9, with bench_instances and history_sessions configs. Evaluation adapts the EverOS pipeline and needs API keys for the answer LLM, the judge LLM and the memory backends. The judge defaults to gemini-3.1-pro-preview-thinking via OpenRouter. The latest arXiv version is v3 (2026-10-05).

sources.venue: arXiv abs page has no comments or journal_ref; paper HTML names no venue; ACL Anthology search and the acl-2026 event page have no BenchTrace entry (checked 2026-10-10). The repo/HF BibTeX 'Proceedings of ACL' is unverified
sources.memory_types: Paper §3.3.2 Evolution Evaluation: the agent receives evolution snapshots (signal snapshot s0 with failure f0 plus noise snapshots), then is run on a test snapshot truncated before failure fd. FAR measures whether past failure experience is reused, including Type 3 where s0 comes from a different subtask, with memory baselines RAG/ReMem/MemRL/AutoSkill (procedural_workflow). name: EgoStream

scale.notes: 2,250 human-validated 4-way multiple-choice questions, drawn from Multi-Hop EgoQA (578), Ego4D EM (498), EgoLife (433), EgoTempo (425) and HD-EPIC (316). They expand into 8,528 recall-conditioned evaluations across 7 recall regimes, from instant (0 s) to ultra-long (>8 h). The paper gives no video count or average video length. The project page lists a maximum Answer Validity Window of 45.3 h.

metrics: Multiple-choice accuracy (4-way; chance 25%), broken down by 7 semantic memory categories and 7 temporal recall regimes, with macro-averages
Memory budget (tokens) / offloading storage (GB x min)
notes: No public data or code as of 2026-10-10. The project page says "DATA COMING SOON" and lists GitHub as "coming soon". The paper mentions an anonymous GitHub repo but gives no URL. saroo25/Egostream only holds the website source. Questions are built on five existing egocentric datasets (Ego4D, EgoLife, EgoTempo, Multi-Hop EgoQA, HD-EPIC), so the source-video licences apply. Gemini 3.1 and Gemini 2.5 Pro helped build the dataset (rewriting, distractors, labels); scoring uses no LLM. The paper's baselines are KV-cache memory policies on Qwen3-VL.

name: GroupMemBench

scale.avg_context_length: ~2.7M tokens per dialogue (paper Table 1 'Avg. Length'); 30,000 messages per domain
scale.notes: conversations = 4 domain corpora (Finance, Technology, Healthcare, Manufacturing). Each corpus is a multi-channel group conversation of 30,000 messages spread over 6-10 project channels (33 channels in total; 120K turns in total per Table 1). Memory stores are built per domain (App. H). questions = 745, the question set released in the repo. This total is the sum of the README count table, and line counts of questions/*/*.jsonl confirm it. By domain: Finance 214, Technology 213, Healthcare 145, Manufacturing 173. By type: multi_hop 182, knowledge_update 107, temporal 162, user_implicit 49, term_ambiguity 106, abstention 139. The paper states no total question count. The Fig. 5 caption gives 185 non-abstention questions per domain, which matches the repo's Finance and Technology counts. Per the README, the Finance and Technology questions are solvability-filtered, while Healthcare and Manufacturing ship the unfiltered generated set. Registry arithmetic on the abstention accuracies in paper Tables 9-10 implies 19 and 33 abstention questions for Healthcare and Manufacturing. The repo has 34 and 48. So the paper's evaluation set may differ slightly from the release (inferred, not stated by the authors).

metrics: Accuracy (%) judged by an LLM against gold answers, per question category (Multi-Hop, Knowledge Update, Term Ambiguity, User-Implicit, Temporal, Abstention) and averaged
Ingestion cost (USD) of LLM + embedding calls during memory construction
Storage footprint (GB) of each baseline's per-domain store
Retrieval recall and P(correct | gold retrieved) (failure analysis)
notes: The conversations are synthetic enterprise group-chat logs generated with GPT-5. Every question is bound to an asking user (asking_user_id). The official repo ships only two RAG baselines, BM25 and text-embedding-3-large, both using a gpt-5 QA agent and a gpt-5 judge. The agent memory systems in paper Table 2 (Mem0, MemGPT, A-Mem, HippoRAG, Hindsight, GraphRAG) are not included. Running the evaluation needs OpenAI or Azure OpenAI API keys (.env). In the paper, memory ingestion uses gpt-4o-mini. The judge's max_tokens is 2048 in the paper (App. I) but 256 in the repo's eval_lib.py. The GitHub repo has no LICENSE file and the HF dataset card declares no licence; the arXiv paper is CC BY 4.0. The HF dataset card links its companion code repo as KimperYang/GroupMemBench, which returns 404; the paper links UCSB-NLP-Chang/GroupMemBench. The HF card lists '~22,000' messages for Healthcare and Manufacturing. However, the HF files have the same byte sizes as the repo files, and the repo files contain 30,000 messages each, matching paper Table 6. The HF dataset holds only the conversation data; the question sets are in the GitHub repo.

name: LongMemEval-V2

scale.notes: questions = 451 (abstract; release: 240 web, 211 enterprise; 134 static, 86 dynamic, 74 workflow, 29 gotchas, 128 abstention). conversations = 1,540 collected agent trajectories (§3.2: 599 WebArena + 941 WorkArena). LME-V2-Small: one 100-trajectory haystack per domain (~25M tokens). LME-V2-Medium: ~500-trajectory question-specific haystacks (~115M tokens; release mean 498, min 387).

metrics: Accuracy (overall and per ability: static, dynamic, workflow, gotchas; deterministic normalized/ordered phrase, single-choice and multi-select matching for structured answers, binary LLM judge for gotchas and abstention)
notes: This is a separate benchmark from LongMemEval (2024). Its histories are multimodal web and ServiceNow agent trajectories, not chats. Paper §3.2 reports a pool of 1,540 trajectories, but the HF trajectories.jsonl (~1.2 GB) holds 1,870 records (counted 2026-10-10), of which the haystacks reference 1,473. Running the harness needs a self-hosted Qwen3.5-9B reader, an OpenAI key for the GPT-5.2 judge, and a Codex binary for the coding-agent baselines. The leaderboard's LAFS-gain score comes from the repo and website only, not the paper. Code and data are Apache-2.0 and ungated.

name: MBench

scale.notes: questions = 1,040 video evaluation samples (paper Table 4): MBench-A 547 (human 120, object 100, causal 100, environment 227) and MBench-T 493 (120/100/200/73). The HF card expands MBench-T causal into 391 condition-level items, giving 684 MBench-T items. Source videos run 5 s to 15 min. Rollouts are 25 s (A) or 5 segments of about 5 s (T). There are no conversations.

metrics: M-Score (harmonic mean of Memory Reliability and Trigger Coverage), reported per sub-dimension
Memory Reliability (mean consistency over triggered samples)
Trigger Coverage (fraction of samples that trigger the memory challenge)
Entity: Human Identity / Human Appearance / Object Texture / Object Geometry consistency
Environment: Spatial Epipolar / Spatial Reprojection / Rendering Style / Rendering Lighting consistency
Causal: Action Instruction (camera) interaction / Text interaction / Self-Evolution State / Self-Evolution Correctness
Trigger-judge vs human agreement: accuracy, precision, recall, F1
notes: This benchmark evaluates video world models (video generators), not LLM agents. Here 'memory' means entity, environment and causal consistency in generated video over long horizons. It has two settings: MBench-A (action-conditioned, 6 models) and MBench-T (text-conditioned, 8 models). The HF dataset is ungated and its card states no licence; the code is MIT. The dataset ships sample metadata, MBench-A source videos and rollouts from 14 models. DA3 camera-pose artifacts are not included. The repo hard-codes no VLM judge.

name: MemEye

scale.notes: conversations = 8 life-scenario tasks, each one multi-session image-grounded dialogue (the paper concatenates 'conversations from different tasks'). Totals are 221 sessions, 848 dialogue rounds and 438 images (Table 3). questions = 371, each in a mirrored MCQ and open-ended form. 60 are Y3 state-revision items. HF also has concat_* files for the cross-topic scaling ablation. A recount of the HF JSON on 2026-10-10 matches.

metrics: Multiple-choice exact-match accuracy (EM), averaged over four answer rotations
Open-ended LLM-as-a-Judge score (normalized semantic correctness in [0,1]; primary metric)
BLEU-1 (auxiliary lexical metric for open-ended answers, Appendix D.1)
Caption-Proof gain (Score_V - Score_T, native-image vs dense-caption memory; diagnostic)
notes: Data is on Hugging Face MemEyeBench/MemEye: ungated, with an Apache-2.0 card. Images come from third-party or generated sources (Pitt Image Ads, Alley Oop comics, Japan Open Driving Dataset, StyleGAN faces, GPT-5.2/DALL-E). The HF card's per-task image counts (e.g. Cartoon 119, Social Chat 67) differ from paper Table 3 (87, 43). The dialogue JSONs, counted on 2026-10-10, match the paper's 438 referenced images. Text-only methods use GPT-5.2 dense captions. The Generative Agents baseline needs MemEngine, which is not bundled. Running and judging need paid APIs.

name: Momento

scale.notes: 161 = multi-session task instances (paper §2.3), matching the 161 rows of the HF scenarios.jsonl test split. The paper reports no session or turn counts. metrics: DB State (final database state matches goal)
Output (response satisfies user request; information coverage)
Tool Recall (correct tools in correct order)
notes: Agentic benchmark: past sessions are seeded into memory, then a tool-using agent (26 restaurant-domain tools, PostgreSQL in Docker) serves an LLM-simulated user (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B in the paper). The paper states a CC-BY-SA dataset licence, but the HF card says CC-BY-4.0. Images ship separately (images.zip). Unrelated to the MEMENTO entry.

name: PrecisionMemBench

scale.notes: 89 scored cases = 77 single-turn retrieval cases (43 active, 25 structural, 9 trivially empty) + 12 turn-level assertions across 2 session scenarios (an 11-turn topic-drift session + a 1-turn cross-session case). conversations = those 2 session scenarios. Fixed seed corpus of 35 beliefs (23 code, 7 writing, 5 universal) plus a secondary-user fixture. Counted in repo fixtures on 2026-10-10.

metrics: Case pass count / pass rate (all mustInclude / mustExclude / shouldOnlyInclude belief-ID assertions satisfied; split into active, structural, trivially-empty passes)
Drift score (fraction of retrieved non-pinned beliefs from off-topic turns, session cases)
notes: arXiv v1 (2026-05-11) had a different title ("Beyond Similarity Search: Tenure...") and a 72-case evaluation; the PrecisionMemBench name and 89-case set appear from v2 (2026-05-27). Retrieval-only: scores returned belief IDs, with no answer generation. The benchmark's author also built Tenure, the system that scores 89/89. Case fixtures are in the GitHub repo (MIT). The HF dataset holds only leaderboard and result files. README results (Sept 2026) were re-run after an adapter fix, and the original reports are kept in test-results/baseline/original/.

The paper says code will go on GitHub and the dataset will be released under CC BY 4.0. The paper also proposes the REMIND method.

name: RoboMemArena

scale.notes: No dialogues or QA items. The benchmark has 26 simulated LIBERO manipulation tasks (4 transferring, 11 occlusion, 7 counting, 4 sequence) with 100 demos each (2,600 trajectories; 15,100 keyframe segments; 151 subtasks, 68.9% memory-dependent). It also has 5 real-world tasks with 10 rollouts each. The official script defaults to 51 trials per task. The paper does not give the number of simulation trials.

notes: Access to the HF dataset is gated with automatic approval (login required; Apache-2.0). A June 20, 2026 update changed the Tasks 1-5 scenes and data and the Task 6 evaluation logic, so it differs from the paper's v1 results. That update shipped on ModelScope first, and the README said the HF mirror was "coming soon". On 2026-10-10 the HF repo held 14,800 subtask HDF5 files, against 15,100 segments in the paper. full_trajectory files are on ModelScope only. Memory is tested within a single episode, not across sessions.

name: SeqMem-Eval

scale.notes: questions = sum of Table 6 sequential-test sizes (HumanEval 132, MATH500 500, MMLU-Pro-Engineering 873, MMLU-Pro-Physics 1170, APIBench-HF 911, ALFWorld 140). ID hold-out sets total 681 (32/280/96/129/120/24). Appendix C.2 adds OOD hold-out on AIME2024, AIME2025 and MMLU-Pro-Physics using MATH500-stream memory. Task streams, not conversations; no context length reported.

notes: SeqMem-Eval is an evaluation framework built on existing public datasets: HumanEval, MATH500, MMLU-Pro Engineering/Physics, APIBench-HF and ALFWorld. The Apache-2.0 repo ships code only, so each dataset must be downloaded from its upstream source. As of 2026-10-10, the repo lacks two things that configs/holdout.py references: the hold-out split files under data/Holdout-data/ and the harness scripts/holdout/run.py. Only sequential online runs through main.py can be reproduced directly. The paper's backbones are Qwen3-8B and MiniMax-M2.7.

name: SkillEvolBench

scale.notes: 180 tasks = 6 environments x 5 skill families x 6 role-conditioned tasks: 3 acquisition (canonical/enriched/variant) and 3 frozen deployment (context-shift/adversarial/composition) per family. Each environment runs as one lifelong episode; there are no conversations. 30 curated seed skills. 180 task dirs in both repo and HF dataset (counted on 2026-10-10).

notes: Agent benchmark, not QA: success comes from deterministic verifiers (public, hidden and process tests). Running it needs Harbor, a Docker runtime image and paid model access (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock Claude or Gemini). name: STALE

scale.notes: 400 = conflict instances (200 Type I co-referential, 200 Type II propagated), each a 50-session user-assistant haystack padded with LongMemEval distractor sessions; 1,200 = 3 probing queries (SR, PR, IPA) per instance. metrics: Accuracy (LLM-judge Boolean pass rate) per conflict type (Type I / Type II) and probing dimension: State Resolution (SR), Premise Resistance (PR), Implicit Policy Adaptation (IPA)
Overall accuracy (average across the six type x dimension settings)
notes: Data on Hugging Face (CC BY 4.0, ungated): one ~306 MB JSON, 400 rows. Repo is MIT-licensed. It also holds the generation pipeline and the CUPMem baseline. Distractor sessions come from LongMemEval (MIT). Models with short context windows are evaluated with evidence-preserving truncation, and memory frameworks use a GPT-4o-mini backbone.

name: STATE-Bench

scale.notes: questions = 150 held-out test tasks (50 per domain: travel, customer support, shopping assistant). Each is a simulated multi-turn conversation, run 5 times. conversations = 300 train trajectories (100 per domain) supplied for learning extraction. There are 450 scenarios in total, and the current main branch ships all 150 task definitions per domain (counted 2026-10-10). No average length is reported.

metrics: Task Completion pass@1 (average over 5 runs; deterministic final-state checks plus an LLM judge for procedural/informational requirements)
Task Completion pass^5 (reliability: tasks passed on all 5 runs)
notes: No accompanying paper was found (arXiv API and web search, 2026-10-10). The benchmark was released through the GitHub repo (first release v0.4.5, 2026-05-20) and the Microsoft Open Source Blog (2026-05-19). Memory is evaluated in the Agent Learning Track, and the Main Track (no learning) uses the same test split. The locked simulator and judge moved from GPT-5.1 to GPT-5.4 in v0.7.0, so official runs need GPT-5.4 access. The data is LLM-generated synthetic data under the MIT licence. Not to be confused with Hugging Face parslee/statebench.

name: SEA-Eval

scale.notes: conversations = 92 task sequences: 32 correlated, 30 orthogonal and 30 implicit-intent (v3 §4.3.4). questions = 32 atomic tasks: 12 Easy, 18 Normal, 2 Hard. Table 1 instead gives 12/18 Easy/Normal sequences for each of Correlated, Orth-Same and Orth-Similar. The experiments use only the Easy sequences. arXiv v1 described a different set: 30 atomic tasks, a 120-task streaming pool, 45 step-changes and 30 preference instances.

metrics: Token Consumption (T/TC, mean K tokens per sequence stage)
Token change rate (R3 vs R1, A2/A3 vs R1; median per agent)
Normalized composite score (Median-AVG / Mean-AVG over 8 dimensions)
notes: The benchmark runs agent frameworks (GenericAgent, OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code, Codex) on live web and OS tasks inside sandboxes. The paper does not describe how task success is checked. The dataset composition changed between arXiv v1 and v2/v3. The official repo's default branch (master) is empty. Its main branch serves the leaderboard page: 12 task groups × 3 variants with Chinese prompts, the interference mapping and per-agent token/status results. It has no Normal/Hard or implicit-intent tasks, answer keys, evaluation script or licence (checked 2026-10-10). The paper reports no implicit-intent, noisy-condition or K_align results.

name: SkillLearnBench

scale.notes: 100 = verified task instances across 20 skill-dependent tasks (15 sub-domains, 6 categories), 2-6 instances per task. A skill set is generated once per task from the seed instance (instance-1) and tested on all instances, including held-out ones. No dialogues. Context length is not reported; the paper gives solving-token cost instead (e.g., 727K avg tokens for no-skill).

metrics: Trajectory alignment (key point recall, execution order, completeness)
notes: 17 of the 20 tasks are adapted from SkillsBench, and 3 are new. The task data (Docker environments, instructions, verifiers and oracle solutions) is stored in the repo's tasks/ folder; there is no separate dataset page. Running the evaluation requires Docker and Anthropic and OpenAI API keys, plus GH_TOKEN for github-repo-analytics. The solving agent is Claude Sonnet 4.6. The repo also ships pre-generated skills for 4 methods x 6 LLMs. MIT licence. 100 task.toml instances counted on 2026-10-10.

name: StratMem-Bench

scale.avg_context_length: ~8.79 memory items per pool (~9.81 words per item)
scale.notes: 657 single-turn instances built from LoCoMo multi-session dialogues. The memory pool comes from 1-3 prior sessions and the history from the next session. Split: 50 must-only, 132 nice-only, 475 must+nice. The number of source conversations is not reported. Averages are from paper Table 1. Dialogue-history length is not reported.

metrics: Memory Integration Quality (MIQ, 1-5 Likert; reported as MIQ on SMC-pass)
notes: The repo has two files with 657 instances each (counted on 2026-10-10). data/StratMemBench.json holds the full memory pools (avg 8.79 items, matching Table 1). data/StratMemBench_testset.json caps nice memories at two per instance (avg 7.5 items), matching the downsampled setting in paper §5.2. No evaluation code is released (me.py is empty). The README licence section reads "To be added", while GitHub lists Apache-2.0. The judge model, DeepSeek-V3.2, is also one of the evaluated models.

name: AMB (Agent Memory Benchmark)

scale.notes: AMB reports no overall total; it bundles 7 datasets. Queries per split (repo data/*/stats.json.gz, counted 2026-10-10): LoCoMo locomo10 1,540 (10 conversations); LongMemEval s 500; BEAM 100k/500k/1m/10m 400/700/700/200; PersonaMem 32k/128k/1M 589/2,727/2,674; LifeBench en 2,003 (10 users); PrecisionMemBench 77 cases; sde-bench boltons 61 tasks.

metrics: Accuracy: binary LLM-judge correctness against gold answers (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, LifeBench)
BEAM rubric-nugget score (0/0.5/1 per nugget, averaged; a query counts as correct at >= 0.5)
Pass rate on must/must-not memory-ID assertions, plus mean precision, mean recall and active passes (PrecisionMemBench, no LLM)
Solve rate (repro, existing and hidden tests all pass under pytest) and corrections (test-feedback retries, cap 5), plus cost in USD and wall time (sde-bench)
notes: There is no paper. AMB is documented only by its repo README and Vectorize's blog manifesto (2026-03-23). Vectorize also develops Hindsight, which leads the AMB leaderboard. Six of the seven datasets repackage third-party benchmarks (LoCoMo without adversarial QA, LongMemEval-S, BEAM, LifeBench, PersonaMem, PrecisionMemBench); only sde-bench is original. The v1 blog also listed MemBench and MemSim, which were absent from the repo on 2026-10-10. Current code defaults BEAM's judge to gemini-3.5-flash. The repo has no LICENSE file; sde-bench is MIT.

name: AMemGym

scale.avg_context_length: 60K to 140K tokens on average (base version; varies by assistant model)
scale.notes: Base config (v1.base): 20 simulated user profiles, each one long-horizon conversation (11 periods; 943 sessions total). 200 multiple-choice questions (10 per user, 4-7 options), each re-asked at 11 positions (2,200 answers). The Extra config (20 users, 420 periods, 1,632 sessions, 512K+ context) appears in the paper but is not on HF.

metrics: Normalized memory score (overall accuracy rescaled between a random baseline and a perfect-memory upper bound)
Memory Factual Recall (R_fact; self-evolution experiment only)
notes: The evaluation is on-policy: the assistant talks live with an LLM-simulated user (gpt-4.1 in the paper; deepseek-v3 is an alternative), so running it requires OpenAI-compatible API access. Answers are scored by multiple-choice option matching, not by an LLM judge. GPT-4.1 judges factual consistency only for the auxiliary R_fact metric in the self-evolution experiment. The HF dataset (CC-BY-4.0, ungated) has only v1.base. The README arXiv badge is still a placeholder.

name: ATM-Bench

scale.notes: questions = 1,038 QA pairs reported in the paper (Table 6: 1,013 ATM-Bench + 25 ATM-Bench-Hard); the released Hard split has 31. No dialogues: a single personal memory corpus of 6,741 emails, 3,759 images and 533 videos (~12k items, Table 1). 2.25M tokens = whole corpus accessible to the agent, with each media item counted as 300 tokens. NIAH pools (25/50/100/200) exist for Hard.

notes: Paper v1 reports 1,038 QAs (1,013 ATM-Bench + 25 ATM-Bench-Hard). The Hugging Face release, counted on 2026-10-10, has 1,013 + 31 Hard questions and 6,742 emails (paper: 6,741), and the README says Hard results on the release set may differ from the preprint. Data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial research only); code is MIT. It is one real user's ~4-year personal corpus. Scoring open-ended answers needs an OpenAI judge (gpt-5-mini).

name: LifeBench

scale.notes: conversations = 10 synthetic users, each with a one-year (2025) multi-source life history: events plus 9 phone-data types such as SMS, calls, agent chats and photos (stored as text metadata). questions = 2,003 QA in paper v1 (IE 718, MR 597, TKU 229, ND 429, UA 30). Release v2.0: 10 users, 3,380 QA, 9 categories (counted on 2026-10-10).

metrics: Accuracy (LLM-as-judge with the LoCoMo evaluation prompt)
Per-category accuracy (IE, MR, TKU, ND, UA)
notes: The paper (arXiv v1) evaluates v1 data: 2,003 QA in 5 categories, kept on the repo's main branch under life_bench_data/version1. The default branch (lifebench2.0) and Hugging Face host v2.0: 3,380 QA in 9 categories, in Chinese and English, Apache-2.0, not gated. Evaluation code lives in a separate repo, 1754955896/LifeBench_eval, which has no licence file. It targets v2.0 and uses a rubric-based judge prompt instead of the paper's LoCoMo prompt. Photos are text metadata, not images.

name: Persona-MME

scale.notes: 200 = synthetic personas, each with one long multi-session multimodal dialogue history; 2,034 = multiple-choice test cases. 32k config (dialogues under 100 turns): 1,129 cases / 100 personas; 128k config: 905 cases / 100 personas (counted on 2026-10-10 from released Persona-MME.json). 15.87% of turns are multimodal; 34.02% of questions need visual information.

metrics: Accuracy (%) on multiple-choice questions (overall, per aspect, per 14 tasks)
Pairwise win/tie/loss rate on open-ended generation (200 sampled questions, LLM-judged)
notes: Introduced in the PersonaVLM paper (repo calls it a CVPR 2026 Highlight). Dialogues are synthetic. Questions were generated with Gemini-2.5-Pro and then manually reviewed. Main results are multiple-choice accuracy. 406 cases add a binary personality-alignment test, scored once on the chosen and once on the rejected response (812 items). Dialogue histories and images are on Hugging Face (Apache-2.0, not gated); the GitHub repo holds only the question JSON. The official eval.py runs only the PersonaVLM agent (Qwen2.5-VL-7B), so other models need adaptation.

name: RMBench

scale.notes: Not a dialogue/QA benchmark. It has 9 simulated manipulation tasks: 5 M(1) and 4 M(n). Each policy trains on 50 demos per task and is evaluated on 100 rollouts per task, so 900 rollouts in total. Real-world: 3 tasks with 100 demos and 40 trials each. The paper gives no episode length. Repo step limits range from 250 to 3500 steps per task.

metrics: Success rate (per task, averaged per memory-complexity level M(1)/M(n), and overall)
notes: Robot-manipulation benchmark in RoboTwin 2.0 simulation. Memory means history of visual observations within an episode. Counted on 2026-10-10, the repo eval list has 10 tasks: it adds place_block_mat, which the paper does not mention. The HF dataset is MIT-licensed and not gated. It holds 50-demo demo_clean zips per task, plus demo_clean_200 sets for 4 tasks. The README links a policy/ folder that is missing from the repo tree. Adapters come through the XPolicyLab submodule. Mem-0 checkpoints were retrained and re-released on 2026-07-14.

name: AMA-Bench

scale.notes: 208 = real-world agent trajectories from 6 domains (Spider 2.0 Text2SQL, GAIA tool QA, WebArena, games, ALFWorld, SWE-bench). 2,496 = their open-ended QA, 12 per trajectory (Recall 839, Causal Inference 596, State Updating 647, State Abstraction 414). A separate synthetic subset has 1,200 QA over BabyAI/TextWorld trajectories in 8K-128K token bins (240 per bin). The maximum trajectory length is 996,826 tokens.

notes: Published at ICML 2026 (PMLR v306). The README also reports an oral at the ICLR 2026 Memory Agent workshop. The Hugging Face release (MIT, ungated) contains only the real-world open-ended subset: 208 trajectories x 12 QA, counted on 2026-10-10. The synthetic BabyAI/TextWorld subset (1,200 QA) is not released as data; only its generation scripts are. run.py accepts an 'mcq' subset that is missing from the release. Paper Table 8 lists 209 selected trajectories, but Table 9 and the release have 208. The README warns that the default Qwen3-32B judge is lenient.

name: ES-MemEval

scale.notes: conversations = 18 multi-session conversations, one per virtual user, with 401 sessions in total. Table 2 also gives 22.3 avg sessions/conv, 23.4 avg turns/session and a 14.9-month avg span; the Intro says about 510 turns and up to 33 sessions. questions = 1,209 QA items: IE 271, TR 236, CD 226, UM 251, Abs 225. Other tasks are summarization (125) and dialogue generation (34 scenarios). The paper reports different session counts in different places: 22.3 avg sessions/conv in Table 2 and 27.2 in Sec 4.3. The released data/evo_emo.json matches the paper on 18 users, 401 sessions, 125 summaries and 34 scenarios, but a registry count of it gives 1,427 QA items, not 1,209.

metrics: LLM ratings 1-5 for LT-Mem., Pers., ES (dialogue generation)
judge_model: GPT-4o (QA, summarization and dialogue-rating judge); Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503 for dialogue-generation observation-based metrics
notes: Domain is emotional support. The EvoEmo dataset has 18 virtual users. Their initial sessions come from ESConv dialogues, and later sessions were generated with GPT-4o from user profiles and event timelines. The paper states the dataset contains no real user conversations and is for research use only, not clinical deployment. Discrepancy: the released data/evo_emo.json holds 1,427 QA items (registry count), while paper Table 2 reports 1,209, and qa_experiment.py scores every item without filtering. The GitHub file and the Zenodo v1.0.0 archive have the same SHA-256. Zenodo is a GitHub release snapshot licensed CC-BY-4.0; the GitHub repo has no LICENSE file. Running the scripts needs an OpenAI API key for the GPT-4o judge and the GPT models, plus vLLM-served Mistral-24B, Ministral-8B and Phi-3-Medium. The community list reported no code link, but the official code exists. The paper evaluates only full-context and RAG baselines (bge-m3 retriever); it does not evaluate dedicated memory systems.

name: LoCoMo-Plus

scale.notes: questions = 401 new 'Cognitive' cue-trigger instances, counted in the official repo's data/locomo_plus.json (causal 101, state 100, goal 100, value 100). The paper text never states an exact count. Figure 2 shows the Cognitive bar at about 425 when read from the chart, but no number is printed, so the released file may not exactly match the evaluated set. conversations = 10 LoCoMo host conversations (data/locomo10.json). Each instance's cue and trigger are inserted as new sessions into one host conversation, placed according to its time_gap. unified_input.py assigns item i to conversation i mod 10, while data/README.md says build_conv.py picks one at random. So every instance gets its own stitched context. The unified evaluation also re-scores LoCoMo's original 1,986 QA from locomo10.json (single-hop 841, multi-hop 282, temporal 321, commonsense 96, adversarial 446), for 2,387 items in total. Average context length is not reported. The length-sensitivity analysis (Sec. 6.5) uses 100 cases per memory type (object / episodic / cognitive).

metrics: LLM-as-judge constraint-consistency score (correct=1, partial=0.5, wrong=0; 3-level labels for single-hop/multi-hop/commonsense, binary for temporal, adversarial and cognitive)
Per-category scores on the 5 LoCoMo categories + LoCoMo average
Gap = LoCoMo average minus LoCoMo-Plus score
EM, token F1, BLEU, ROUGE (evaluation-bias analysis only)
PDR (Precision Decay Ratio) and RTR (Recall Terminal Ratio) for length sensitivity
notes: LoCoMo-Plus adds a sixth 'Cognitive' category to LoCoMo. It tests implicit constraints (causal / state / goal / value) where the later trigger is worded very differently from the earlier cue. Cognitive items have no reference answer: an LLM judge checks whether the response acknowledges or adapts to the cue. The ACL 2026 camera-ready adds a 'Note on Judge Stability' that is not in arXiv v1: some closed-source judge models gave slightly different results from the original submission, and the authors plan to release an open-source judge (not in the repo as of 2026-10-10). The repo's judge.sh defaults to gpt-4o-mini, not the paper's gemini-2.5-flash, and it needs an OpenAI-compatible API. The repo has no LICENSE file. It redistributes LoCoMo's locomo10.json, and upstream snap-research/locomo is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. The paper says per-instance human annotations and judge rationales are released in the repo, but the current tree has none: the judged output files were deleted in commits on 2026-02-11. Open issues reported by users and not answered: #2 says some cue_dialogue lines are malformed (registry check: 44 of 401 cue strings with no real newline, 31 of them containing a literal '\n'); #3 says the cognitive inputs have no session timestamps. The model_name field in locomo_plus.json (e.g. gpt-5.1, gpt-4o-mini) does not fully match the generator list in Appendix A. There is no official Hugging Face dataset; issue #1 asks for one.

name: Neuromem

scale.notes: conversations = the 10 LoCoMo conversations ('10 core tasks', App. A.3), the set used for the full D1-D5 ablation. No question counts or context lengths are reported for any reused dataset. LongMemEval-Oracle tasks are concatenated into one stream, and the MemoryAgentBench Selective Forgetting subset is used only to cross-validate D1 trends.

metrics: F1 degradation across rounds (R1 to R5)
notes: Neuromem is an evaluation testbed and streaming protocol, not a new dataset. It re-serializes LoCoMo, LongMemEval (Oracle subset) and MemoryAgentBench (Selective Forgetting subset) into an interleaved insert/retrieve stream and scores 5 rounds at 20% intervals. Full ablations cover LoCoMo only. Backbones: pangu-1b and Llama-3.1-8B. As checked on 2026-10-10, the public repo contains only LoCoMo loaders and data, with no LongMemEval or MemoryAgentBench adapters. The repo moved from intellistream/neuromem-bench, which redirects to it.

name: PersistBench

scale.notes: questions = 500 human-validated samples (200 cross-domain leakage, 200 sycophancy, 100 beneficial memory use), each a memory set plus one query. There are no dialogue histories, so conversations is null. The §5.3 multi-turn robustness check embeds 150 queries in simulated conversations. Release files counted 2026-10-10: 500/200/200/100 lines, mean 10.6 memories.

metrics: Failure rate (FR, %) for cross-domain leakage, with 95% bootstrap CI (LLM-judge score 1-5, >=3 = failure, failure if any of 3 generations fails)
Failure rate (FR, %) for memory-induced sycophancy, with 95% bootstrap CI (LLM-judge score 1-5, >=3 = failure, any of 3 generations)
Failure rate (FR, %) for beneficial memory use (LLM-judge score 1-3, >=2 = failure, 1 generation)
notes: The main evaluation is single-turn: user memories go in the system prompt, followed by one query. 18 LLMs evaluated. The repo README recommends the Inspect-native implementation (UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals, persistbench). The repo's beneficial judge prompt scores 3 = pass, and analysis/failure_rates.py counts only a score of 1 as failure. Paper §4.3 instead uses 1 = best, with >=2 as failure. No licence file in the repo. An unrelated Hugging Face dataset, 'PersistBenchDataset' (4D foundation models), shares the name.
